short_answer: Dave Essler is a real, active seller on Pregame.com, one of the best known pick marketplaces. His pro page lists ten packages with prices, a daily message and his most recent picks with results, and Pregame staff and members have discussed him on its forum since at least 2015. In that sense the service is legitimate.

Whether the picks make money over time is a different question. The top of his page shows streaks such as "367-229 (62%) GOM Winners" and "86% NFL 3* Totals," chosen for display. The Win/Loss table we saw, in its default view, showed 45 wins and 33 losses with a weighted gain of $693, including 7 wins and 11 losses in the NFL. Pregame's full archive of his picks sits behind a captcha, so we could not audit it.

Treat Dave Essler as an experienced seller with selected marketing numbers, not a proven long term winner. If you buy, use the Pregame archive to read his full record for the sport you want, and log every pick yourself with the line you actually got.

guarantee: None of the ten packages on the Dave Essler page mentions a guarantee, a refund or free extra time. The Pregame FAQ we read covers purchased picks, discounts and forum moderation, and the only protection it describes is an "opposite side insurance" program for buyers who bought two pros on opposite sides of the same game.

The Pregame terms say Pregame does not "WARRANT, ENDORSE, GUARANTEE, OR ASSUME RESPONSIBILITY" for products offered by third parties through the service. Read the checkout terms before you pay, and note that the Flex Access package rebills every month until you cancel by email. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered.

claims_note: Every number at the top of the page is a streak or a best slice. The page itself labels the table "Best W/L Records," and the streak box mixes win rates, unit totals and star ratings without saying when each run starts. The NBA run is shown as 99.65 in the streak box and 99.60 in the daily message on the same day.

The bio does not claim a long record or big winnings. In it he writes that few bettors make a living, that he "made my living in a former life," and that he tells long term clients "we are not going to retire betting on sports." That is more modest than most sales pages in this business.
record: What a buyer can check: Pregame shows an Every Pick Ever archive for him, split into monitored picks that count in the W/L records and unmonitored picks that count for contests only. When we opened it, the page asked for a captcha, so we did not read the full log.

What we saw on the Win/Loss Record page, in its default view: CBB 2 and 1, CFB 17 and 11, CFL 1 and 0, MLB 2 and 0, NBA 12 and 8, NFL 7 and 11, NHL 4 and 2, for 45 wins, 33 losses and a weighted $693. The page text did not make the time frame of the default view clear to us. The Last 10 Picks table on the pro page showed a loss on Dallas Cowboys +4 on 15 Nov 2026 and a win on a team total on 13 Nov 2026, among others.
These figures are graded by Pregame, the marketplace that sells his packages. That is better than no log at all, but it is not an independent audit.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Dave Essler pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Dave Essler performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the streaks on his page run from 55% to 86% winners. On the Watchdog board on 16 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent buyer comment on Dave Essler is thin. Most of what we found sits on the Pregame forum, which is run by the site that sells his picks. Below is everything we could open and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found only a handful of buyer posts, from 2015, 2023 and 2024, on the Pregame forum and TheRX. The tone is mostly friendly: members say his picks paid them on a given weekend, praise his free content and call him a long term winner, though one admits he is not sure of that. Nobody posted a full record, and we found no detailed complaint about the picks. The one public controversy was a 2015 Pregame suspension over a tweet, not over results.

In the Pregame forum thread about his suspension, one member said Essler had recently put money in his pocket and gives solid information, while adding he was not sure Essler is a long term winner and that he does not follow any capper blindly.

In the same thread another member called him a long term winner and argued that a tweet mattered less than a different Pregame capper being 350 units down in 2013. A third member said he is probably among the top three sellers on the site and gives some of the best free content in the forum.
On the Pregame forum, a member who said he rarely buys big plays thanked Nover and Essler for coming through for him that weekend. He gave no stakes or results beyond that.

In a TheRX thread for shared pick buying groups, a member offered access to Essler's NFL package and a Fezzik all access package to anyone interested. It shows people split his subscriptions, but says nothing about results.

The Reddit archive we use (Arctic Shift) refused our searches for Essler on 16 Nov 2026 with a "slow down" timeout on every try, so this page has no Reddit posts. Older Sportsbook Review threads about his plays redirected to the forum home page and did not open. We found no Better Business Bureau, court or regulator record naming him in our searches.

conflicts: Pregame.com sells his packages, grades his record and runs the forum where most comments about him appear. Its forum also places new posters in moderation, per the FAQ. Comments there are not independent of the seller.

In February 2015 a forum post speaking for Pregame announced that Dave Essler had been suspended for 10 days after bashing a Seton Hall player on Twitter, that he had deleted the tweet and apologized, and that the community had in net benefited from his participation. It was a conduct issue, not a complaint about picks.
The 2015 member comment that he is among the top sellers on Pregame is one person's guess, but it fits the size of his package list. A seller's popularity is not evidence that the picks win.
strengths: Sold through a large, known marketplace with a published price for every package.
Pregame keeps a graded archive of his monitored picks and shows recent losses as well as wins on his page.
His bio is unusually frank that few bettors make a living and that clients should keep expectations reasonable.
concerns: Every headline number is a streak or a best slice chosen for display.
No guarantee or refund terms found, and the Flex package rebills monthly until cancelled by email.
Large list prices next to sale prices ($5,000 shown against $885) make discounts look bigger than any real price paid.
The default Win/Loss view we saw had his NFL picks at 7 and 11, down $1,330 weighted, while the page advertises NFL streaks.
Almost all buyer comment sits on the seller's own forum.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real, long running seller on Pregame.com with published prices and a pick archive graded by Pregame. We could not verify that his picks win over time, and we found no court or regulator action involving him. Pregame suspended him for 10 days in 2015 over a tweet about a college player.
How much does Dave Essler cost?
On 16 Nov 2026 his Pregame page sold 7 days of all access for $119.00, 30 days for $249.00, 90 days for $449.00 and one year for $1,995.00, with sport season packages from $449.00 to $885.00.
Does Dave Essler have a verified record?

Not by us. Pregame grades his monitored picks and keeps an archive, but the sales page shows selected streaks, and the archive asked us for a captcha. The default Win/Loss view we saw showed 45 wins and 33 losses.

You get every pick he releases in the period you buy, with written analysis, from a seller who is open about the limits of betting. What is unproven is whether his picks beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays, and we found no refund if they do not.
